hook: Dolgov has been inside Google and Waymo's self-driving effort from its earliest days as a Google X project through its emergence as the first company to operate paid, fully driverless rides at commercial scale, rising from founding engineer to Co-CEO across that entire arc.
name: Dmitri Dolgov

quote.text: Full autonomy is still one of the hardest technology problems of our time.
quote.context: Attributed in Waymo public communications and interviews on the complexity of driverless technology

reading.body:
Dmitri Dolgov is the engineer most directly responsible for the technical path from Google's early self-driving experiment to the first commercially operating, fully driverless robotaxi service, a span of more than a decade inside a single continuous project.

He joined in 2009 as a founding engineer, held the CTO role through the years when Waymo converted test mileage into a commercial product, and reached the 2020 milestone that the data marks as the first no-safety-driver rides offered to paying passengers in Phoenix. That sequence matters because it is unusually unbroken. Most deep-technology programs cycle through multiple technical leaders before reaching commercial operation. Dolgov's elevation to Co-CEO in 2023 extended the same continuity into the executive layer.

The data covers his role and his trajectory but does not cover fleet size, revenue, the compute infrastructure behind Waymo's perception and planning systems, or the power and facility requirements of operating driverless vehicles at scale. His own quoted position, that full autonomy remains one of the hardest technology problems of the time, is consistent with a fifteen-year timeline that has produced commercial service in a limited geography rather than broad deployment. What the data establishes is who held technical accountability across that arc, not how far the arc ultimately reaches.

achievements.title: Founding engineer, Google self-driving car project (2009)
achievements.impact: One of the small original team that built the technology underlying Waymo.

achievements.title: Chief Technology Officer, Waymo
achievements.impact: Directed the engineering behind Waymo's driving software and sensor systems as the company scaled from test vehicles to commercial robotaxi service.

achievements.title: Waymo's fully driverless commercial launch (Phoenix, 2020)
achievements.impact: Under his technical leadership, Waymo became the first company to offer rider-only, no-safety-driver rides to the public.

achievements.title: Named Co-CEO of Waymo (2023)
achievements.impact: Elevated to joint chief executive as Waymo expanded driverless service to additional U.S. cities.
